newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Boiler explodes at Indonesia Dumai refinery - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boiler explodes at Indonesia Dumai refinery - paper.

text.p: A boiler at Indonesian state-owned oil firm Pertamina's Dumai refinery in South Sumatra exploded early on Friday but the fire was put out an hour later, Kompas newspaper reported on Sunday.
Pertamina officials at the 125,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery were not immediately available for comment.
It was unclear whether the fire had affected production.

Kompas said the boiler exploded and then caught fire early on Friday, but Pertamina employees on duty managed to put out the fire an hour later. It said the company's other employees went to work as usual on Friday.
"The explosion triggered panic among the local people because it could be heard as far as 25 km (16 miles) away," said Kompas, adding that an investigation was underway.
The newspaper quoted Pertamina officials as saying the boiler was located in the refinery's vacuum distillation unit.
The Dumai refinery, one of the biggest owned by Pertamina, was inaugurated by President Suharto in 1978.
Pertamina shut down the refinery's crude distillation unit on February 22 for scheduled maintenance and re-started it on March 21.-- Jakarta Newsroom + 6221 384-6364
